passage: Teacher's note, project week. I asked Afreen whether she had used an AI helper for her project on rainwater. She looked at her shoes and said, "No—" and stopped. After a moment she said, "I did. I asked it how rain forms, but the drawing and the paragraph about our tank at home are mine." I thanked her for telling me and asked to see her rough notes. Her hands stayed tight on the folder until I said I cared more about what she understood than about whether she had used help. We agreed she will add one line to the project saying what the assistant helped with. Next step: sit with her on Thursday and look at how to check what a helper tells her. — Ms Jagdish

qa.q: What did Afreen say she made herself?
qa.a: She said the drawing and the paragraph about our tank at home were hers.

qa.q: What might Afreen have been feeling when she began with "No" and stopped?
qa.a: She seems torn between the temptation to deny it and unease about hiding it; her downward look and tight hands suggest nervousness, though that is not certain.

qa.q: How did Ms Jagdish's reply make honesty easier for Afreen?
qa.a: She thanked Afreen, said she cared more about understanding than about whether help was used, and agreed a line crediting the assistant. 👍

qa.q: How might Ms Jagdish see Afreen's first "No"?
qa.a: As a moment of hesitation rather than a fixed lie, since Afreen corrected herself and gave a chance for guidance.

grounding: A child tempted to deny using an AI tells the teacher honestly what she did and did not do herself, keeping trust.

passage:
In Durban, Zanele's frog project lay on Mrs. Mokoena's desk: a pond map, drawings of tadpoles, and a first paragraph that sounded far too grown-up.
"Zanele," Mrs. Mokoena said quietly after class, "did you use an AI for any of this?"
Zanele's mouth went dry. Her classmate Tuan was waiting at the door. Saying no would be so easy.
"Yes," she said. "For the opening paragraph. I asked it to make my words sound better. But I measured the pond myself, and I drew all the tadpoles."
Mrs. Mokoena nodded slowly. "Thank you for telling me. Your drawings are wonderful. Write the opening again in your own words, and next time you can use it to check your spelling."
Zanele walked out with her shoulders loose.

qa.q: Which part did Zanele say the AI had written?
What was Zanele feeling when Mrs. Mokoena asked her question?
qa.a: She felt nervous and tempted; her mouth went dry and saying no seemed so easy.

qa.q: Why was Zanele's honest answer the wiser choice?
qa.a: It kept Mrs. Mokoena's trust, earned real praise for her drawings and brought clear guidance on how to use the AI.

qa.q: How does Mrs. Mokoena see Zanele's honesty?
qa.a: She respects it and answers with thanks and helpful guidance instead of punishment.

grounding: A girl asked by her teacher whether she used AI is tempted to deny it but explains honestly, which keeps trust and lets the teacher guide her.

passage:
At the school science fair, Indu's water-filter model stood on Table 6 with a neat chart beside it. Ms. Fernandes stopped and read the chart twice.
"Indu, did an AI help write this?"
"No, Ma'am," Indu said, too fast. Her partner Vikas looked at his shoes.
Ms. Fernandes moved on to the next table. Indu's cheeks prickled. The chart had come from the AI. She and Vikas had built the filter, tested the gravel layers and timed the drips, but the words weren't hers.
Before the judges arrived, she walked over. "Ma'am, I said no, but that wasn't true. The AI wrote the chart. We did the model and the tests."
Ms. Fernandes smiled. "Thank you for coming back. Explain the tests to the judges yourself. That part is all yours."

qa.q: What did Indu and Vikas build for the fair?
Why did Indu's cheeks prickle after she said no?
qa.a: She felt guilty and uneasy, knowing the chart had come from the AI.

qa.q: How did Indu fix her first answer, and why did it help?
qa.a: She went back before the judges arrived and told the truth, which kept her teacher's trust and let her show her own tests.

qa.q: How might Ms. Fernandes see Indu coming back?
qa.a: She sees an honest student who corrected herself, so she thanks her and guides her to present her real work.

grounding: A girl first denies using AI to her teacher, then honestly explains how she used it and what she did herself, keeping trust.
